what.text: A use case model shows the system from the user's point of view: what the system does.

actor.text: An actor is anyone or anything outside the system that interacts with it. A person, an organization, another system, a device, even time. Name it with a noun.

uc.text: A use case is one unit of meaningful work. Name it with a verb phrase: log in to system, create order.

primary.text: The primary actor starts the use case to reach a goal, like the cashier recording a sale. A supporting actor helps, like the credit bureau authorizing the card.

diagram.text: In the diagram, the actor is a stick figure, the use case is an oval, and the system boundary is a box. A plain line, the association, joins an actor to a use case.

include.text: Include: the base use case always calls the child. A dotted arrow, labeled include, points from the base to the included use case.

extend.text: Extend: optional extra behavior, triggered by a condition. Calculate bonus extends deposit funds, only for deposits over ten thousand. The base must make sense on its own.

general.text: Generalization: a parent and a child, drawn with a hollow triangle pointing to the parent.

scenario.text: Each use case also gets a written scenario, the fully dressed use case: name, actors, trigger, preconditions, postconditions, normal flow, alternate flows, and business rules.
